cases.title: Resolve relative asset URLs without mutating the base
cases.mechanism: Constructor host-op base resolution and hierarchical path normalization
cases.hypothesis: The URL host seam may resolve a relative reference against the full base path or accidentally retain the old query and fragment.
cases.application_relevance: Workers commonly derive resource and redirect targets from a request or configured base URL.
trace: Construct one URL base with nondefault port, path, query, and fragment.
Construct one child with parent-directory and current-directory segments plus its own query and fragment.
Assert the exact child href and components, then the unchanged base href.
cases.desired_behavior: Child is https://route.example.test:8443/docs/assets/icon.svg?theme=dark#outline; base is unchanged.
cases.source_observation: Constructor delegates to the Rust url crate with a parsed base. This is coverage of the host seam, not a predicted failure.
cases.distinctness: Base-relative constructor resolution; no setter, query-list mutation, or URLPattern operation is the mechanism under test.
fixed_runtime_assertions: t.equal(child.href, 'https://route.example.test:8443/docs/assets/icon.svg?theme=dark#outline', 'relative path resolved against base directory');
t.equal(child.origin, 'https://route.example.test:8443', 'base authority inherited');
t.equal(child.pathname, '/docs/assets/icon.svg', 'relative dot segments removed');
t.equal(child.search, '?theme=dark', 'new query replaces base query');
t.equal(child.hash, '#outline', 'new fragment replaces base fragment');
t.equal(base.href, 'https://route.example.test:8443/docs/v1/index.html?old=yes#intro', 'base object unchanged');

cases.title: Encode pathname setter data without changing query or fragment
cases.mechanism: Path setter percent-encoding and component separation
cases.hypothesis: The pathname setter may copy Unicode and reserved path data directly into href, changing the meaning after reparsing.
cases.application_relevance: Workers compose file paths while preserving independent download-query and fragment state.
trace: Construct one HTTPS URL with an existing query and fragment.
Assign /café/report?draft#notes as pathname data.
Assert encoded pathname, unchanged query and fragment, exact href, and fixed pathname after reparse.
cases.desired_behavior: Path becomes /caf%C3%A9/report%3Fdraft%23notes, with ?download=yes#keep remaining independent.
cases.source_observation: Pinned pathname setter only removes ASCII line separators, optionally prepends slash, and copies the value. No percent-encoding step is visible. Source discrepancy hypothesis only.
cases.distinctness: Path-data encoding is independent of host canonicalization, numeric port conversion, and empty-delimiter preservation.
fixed_runtime_assertions: t.equal(url.pathname, '/caf%C3%A9/report%3Fdraft%23notes', 'path setter encodes path data');
t.equal(url.search, '?download=yes', 'path question mark does not start a query');
t.equal(url.hash, '#keep', 'path hash does not start a fragment');
t.equal(url.href, 'https://files.example.test/caf%C3%A9/report%3Fdraft%23notes?download=yes#keep', 'serialized setter result');
t.equal(new URL(url.href).pathname, '/caf%C3%A9/report%3Fdraft%23notes', 'setter serialization survives reparsing');

cases.title: Parse bracketed IPv6 host replacements and their ports
cases.mechanism: Host setter IPv6 bracket awareness and scheme-default port handling
cases.hypothesis: Splitting host at the first colon may corrupt a valid IPv6 literal and its port.
cases.application_relevance: Ordinary Worker endpoint configuration may use documentation-range IPv6 literals without making a network request.
trace: Construct an HTTPS URL with existing port, path, query, and fragment.
Replace host with [2001:db8::7]:8443 and assert hostname, port, host, and href.
Replace with [2001:db8::8]:443 and assert default-port elision and origin.
cases.desired_behavior: IPv6 brackets are preserved as part of hostname; only the colon after the closing bracket separates port.
cases.source_observation: Pinned host setter uses indexOf(':'), without bracket handling. Source discrepancy hypothesis only.

t.equal(url.href, 'https://[2001:db8::7]:8443/path?q=1#part', 'IPv6 setter keeps path and query');
t.equal(url.port, '', 'default IPv6 port is elided');
t.equal(url.origin, 'https://[2001:db8::8]', 'IPv6 origin after default-port elision');

cases.title: Keep a live query view across href replacement
cases.mechanism: URL href replacement and same-object query-list rebinding
cases.hypothesis: Replacing href may detach a previously obtained searchParams object or leave an existing iterator reading the old list.
cases.application_relevance: A Worker can retain a local query view while replacing a redirect URL within one synchronous request.
trace: Construct URL and save its query view and entries iterator.
Consume exactly one old tuple.
Replace href with a different authority and two-entry query.
Assert query object identity, replacement tuples, and the next existing-iterator tuple.
Append through the old view, assert new href and iterator tail, then exhaustion.
cases.desired_behavior: The original view remains the same object bound to the new URL, and the iterator retains its index over the updated list.
cases.source_observation: Pinned _apply refreshes the existing query list. This case checks cross-object identity and iterator wiring; no observed runtime verdict.
cases.distinctness: Whole-URL replacement rebinding; U214 instead mutates an independent params list through its own API.
fixed_runtime_assertions: t.deep(cursor.next(), { value: ['old', '1'], done: false }, 'consume one item before href replacement');
t.equal(url.searchParams === live, true, 'href replacement preserves query object identity');
t.deep([...live], [['first', 'a'], ['second', 'b']], 'existing view sees replacement query');
t.deep(cursor.next(), { value: ['second', 'b'], done: false }, 'existing iterator keeps index in replaced list');
t.equal(url.href, 'https://after.example.test:8443/new?first=a&second=b&last=c#next', 'existing query object stays bound to replacement URL');
t.deep(cursor.next(), { value: ['last', 'c'], done: false }, 'preexisting iterator sees later append');
t.equal(cursor.next().done, true, 'finite iterator reaches completion');

cases.application_relevance: Workers that rewrite a path must not silently change a URL serialized with explicit empty query or fragment markers.

Set only pathname and assert both delimiters remain.
Clear query, then fragment, and assert each serialized state.
Assign search = ? and assert empty-present query serialization.
cases.desired_behavior: The href sequence is /path?#, /next?#, /next#, /next, /next? while empty query and fragment getters remain empty strings.

Delete only empty tag values and verify.
Delete remaining tag values by name and assert only x remains.

t.equal(params.has('tag', 'blue'), true, 'other duplicate values remain');
t.equal(params.has('tag', ''), false, 'empty filter removes empty values only');
t.deep([...params], [['x', '1']], 'name-only delete removes remaining values');

cases.title: Keep a live params iterator current across a temporary list end
cases.mechanism: Web IDL pair-iterator liveness and list-length rechecking
cases.hypothesis: An iterator may snapshot the initial list, retain a deleted tuple, miss an updated value, or latch completion instead of rechecking the list.
cases.application_relevance: Workers may adjust query fields while performing one bounded traversal.
trace: Create params a,b,c and consume one tuple.
Delete unseen b and append d; assert next tuple c.
Update unseen d and assert updated tuple.
Observe done, append e, assert the same iterator yields e and then reports done again; verify fresh iterator final keys.
cases.desired_behavior: Existing iterator yields a,c,updated d, reports done, then yields e after append and reports done again. Web IDL pair iterators do not latch a completed state.
cases.source_observation: Pinned generator uses dynamic length during traversal but latches completion when its body ends; Web IDL pair next instead rechecks the target list on every call. Source discrepancy hypothesis only.
cases.distinctness: Iterator state across direct list mutation; U206 instead replaces an owning URL record.
fixed_runtime_assertions: t.deep(cursor.next(), { value: ['a', '1'], done: false }, 'first iterator yield');
t.deep(cursor.next(), { value: ['c', '3'], done: false }, 'iterator reads current list after removal of unseen entry');
t.deep(cursor.next(), { value: ['d', 'updated'], done: false }, 'iterator sees value changed before yield');
t.equal(cursor.next().done, true, 'iterator completes at current end');
t.deep(cursor.next(), { value: ['e', '5'], done: false }, 'pair iterator rechecks the list after previously reporting done');
t.equal(cursor.next().done, true, 'iterator reports done again at the new end');
t.deep([...params.keys()], ['a', 'c', 'd', 'e'], 'fresh iterator sees final list');

cases.title: Resolve URLPattern base inputs and preserve result input arguments

Match one relative input with an uppercase-host, explicit-default-port base.

Assert a valid URL under another path is a nonmatch.

cases.title: Represent optional URLPattern captures and isolate exec result objects

cases.hypothesis: An unmatched group may be omitted or represented as empty string, or mutation of one result may affect later matches.

Reject a valid URL with an extra segment and assert no custom regexp groups.
cases.desired_behavior: Absent optional id is an own property with undefined value; result edits do not affect a later exec.
